title: Order Service Latency & Database Pool Exhaustion
investigation_steps: Check recent order-service deployment configs for changes in `max_connections` or `maximumPoolSize`
Query active connection count in PostgreSQL pg_stat_activity
Inspect slow query log for locks on orders / order_items tables
mitigation_steps: Roll back to previous stable order-service deployment if pool configuration was reduced
Increase max pool size in Helm values configmap to 50
Restart order-service pods to reinitialize connection pool
escalation_path: Escalate to Order Domain Lead & DBA on-call

title: Relational Database CPU Saturation & Query Optimization
symptoms: High CPU usage on primary DB node
Slow query warnings with Sequential Scan
investigation_steps: Run `SELECT pid, query, state, age(clock_timestamp(), query_start) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state != 'idle' ORDER BY age DESC LIMIT 5;`
Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on longest running queries to check for missing indexes
Identify calling microservice from query comments or connection application_name
mitigation_steps: Terminate long-running unindexed query using `SELECT pg_cancel_backend(pid);`
Create missing index concurrently: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ...`
Set user-level statement_timeout to 10000ms

title: PostgreSQL Connection Exhaustion & Transaction Leaks
symptoms: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved
investigation_steps: Query `SELECT pid, state, age(clock_timestamp(), xact_start) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'idle in transaction';`
Inspect payment-service application traces for missing `@Transactional` boundary closure or unclosed connections
Check client connection pool leak detection logs
mitigation_steps: Terminate stuck idle connections via `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid);`
Configure `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = '15s'` in database
Restart application instances leaking connections
escalation_path: Escalate to Payment Core Team & DBRE

title: Memory Leaks and OOMKilled Pod Crash Recovery
alert_trigger: Pod restart with ExitCode 137 (OOMKilled) OR Memory utilization > 90%
investigation_steps: Capture heap dump / pprof memory profile before pod terminates
Check Git diff of recent releases for unbounded collections or missing cache eviction policies
Verify memory limits in Kubernetes deployment spec
mitigation_steps: Temporarily increase pod memory limits in deployment spec to prevent crash loop
Roll back to prior release without the memory leak
Deploy hotfix configuring bounded cache size with TTL expiration

title: Redis Memory Saturation & Eviction Policy Triage
symptoms: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'
investigation_steps: Check `redis-cli INFO memory` and inspect `maxmemory_policy`
Run `redis-cli --bigkeys` or `redis-cli MEMORY USAGE <key>` to find memory hog keys
Check if background sync job wrote keys without TTL
mitigation_steps: Change eviction policy online: `CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru`
Flush temporary non-critical keyspaces if safe
Scale Redis cluster memory allocation

title: Kafka Producer Connection & Configuration Troubleshooting
investigation_steps: Inspect environment variables and ConfigMap for notification-service
Verify DNS resolution of Kafka bootstrap broker address from inside the pod using nslookup / nc
Review recent Helm/Kustomize deployment commits
mitigation_steps: Correct misspelled hostname in ConfigMap / Helm values
Rollback release to last known working revision
Verify pod status reaches 1/1 Running

title: API Gateway Circuit Breakers & Ingress Routing
alert_trigger: Gateway 503 error rate > 5% while upstream service reports 200 OK
symptoms: CircuitBreaker is OPEN and does not permit further calls
investigation_steps: Check gateway circuit breaker status dashboard / admin metrics endpoint
Inspect half-open probe and waitDuration configuration settings
Check if a transient network glitch previously tripped the threshold
mitigation_steps: Issue manual circuit breaker reset command via admin API
Fix circuit breaker configuration to allow proper half-open self-healing transitions
Reload gateway configuration without dropping active connections

title: SSL/TLS Certificate Expiration & Renewal Troubleshooting
investigation_steps: Check cert-manager certificate resource status: `kubectl describe certificate`
Check cert-manager controller logs for renewal webhook authentication errors
Verify expiration date with `openssl s_client -connect ...`
mitigation_steps: Force manual certificate renewal via cert-manager CLI or Secret update
Rollout restart ingress controller and sidecar proxies to load new cert
Fix webhook authentication token in Secret Manager
escalation_path: Escalate to Security Operations & PKI Lead
